record.question:
A company uses AWS Organizations to manage development accounts. Its security team maintains a list of approved AMI IDs for each Region. Developers must be allowed to launch instances from other AMIs, but security must receive a notification when a running instance is evaluated as noncompliant. No automatic blocking or termination is required.

Which solution meets these requirements with the least custom code?

options.text: Attach an SCP that denies ec2:RunInstances unless the requested AMI is approved, and send notifications for denied API requests.
Enable Amazon Inspector and treat every instance without a vulnerability finding as compliant with the approved AMI list.
Create an AWS Config aggregator in the security account and supply the approved AMI IDs to the aggregator without deploying evaluation rules in source accounts.

Enable AWS Config recording and deploy the approved-amis-by-id managed rule in each relevant account and Region. Match noncompliant rule-evaluation events with EventBridge and send notifications through SNS.

explanation.text:
<<4>> is correct. The `approved-amis-by-id` managed rule evaluates running EC2 instances against its configured AMI IDs. Config compliance events can be matched by EventBridge and delivered to SNS. This is a detective control applied after the resource exists, so it does not block development deployments.

<<1>> is preventive and violates the requirement to permit launches.

<<2>> checks a different property. A vulnerability assessment does not establish that an instance uses an approved image ID.

<<3>> aggregates existing configuration and compliance data but does not replace source-account recording and rule evaluation.

Deploy the rule with the appropriate regional list and verify the event and notification configuration. Config events use best-effort delivery, so a compliance dashboard or reconciliation process can complement operational alerts.

Official AWS references (checked September 18, 2026): [Approved AMI managed rule](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/approved-amis-by-id.html). [Config events with EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/monitor-config-with-cloudwatchevents.html).

diagram_alt: Post-launch Config evaluation routes noncompliant AMI results to notifications without blocking deployment.

editorial_notes: Preserved answer 4. Scoped requirement to post-launch detection and notification, clarified regional rule deployment, and avoided promising guaranteed EventBridge delivery.
